## v2.9.0-beta.1 Release notes

> This is a **preview (Beta)** release for collecting feedback before the stable release. It is offered only when Settings → Global settings → Update channel is set to Preview, and does not affect stable-channel users. Please report problems in Issues with a sanitized `app.log`.

Adds a chain mode for running alongside Clash/Mihomo. Fixes TUN mode restarting repeatedly on some networks and blocked-domain records being cleared. Includes a set of security hardening fixes, sing-box 1.14.4, and Wails 3.0.0.

### Please help test

- **TUN restart loop (#109)**: on networks that provide IPv6 (for example some phone hotspots), TUN mode restarted itself every ten-odd seconds. Start TUN on a network where this happened and check whether it still restarts.
- **Blocked-domain records (#106)**: with automatic expiry turned off, records should stay until you remove them, and removed or cleared records should not come back.
- **Clash/Mihomo chain mode**: new feature; feedback is welcome.

### TUN and network changes

- Fixed TUN mode restarting repeatedly: on some networks Windows stops reporting an adapter's IPv6 DNS while the TUN runs. HypoMux treated this as a network change and restarted, which repeated after every restart. An emptied DNS list no longer triggers a restart; only a new set of DNS servers rebuilds the bindings.
- When a network change triggers an automatic rebuild, the log records which adapter and which field changed (without addresses).
- Repeated automatic rebuilds (more than 3 in 10 minutes) are paused with a notice and resume automatically later, instead of keeping the network down.

### Clash/Mihomo chain mode (new)

- Settings → Local proxy gains a chain setup dialog: Clash keeps the system proxy, its TUN and rules, while node connections are aggregated across adapters through HypoMux's SOCKS5 port, so the two apps no longer compete for system settings. It generates a Mihomo extend script or YAML, plus a sing-box outbound.
- When HypoMux owns the TUN, one click adds aggregation rules for running proxy cores (Mihomo, FlClash, Xray/V2Ray, Hiddify, NekoBox). Rules you already pointed elsewhere are left untouched.
- Clash direct traffic can also be aggregated by HypoMux; LAN and private ranges, and direct rules pinned by process, source or inbound, stay direct. This can be turned off in the dialog.
- The dialog shows live which proxy cores pass through HypoMux. If HypoMux is unavailable, Clash falls back to direct within about 30 seconds.

### Domain isolation and blocked-domain records

- Fixed blocked-domain records being erased by runtime expiry or partial telemetry when automatic expiry is turned off.
- Fixed removed or cleared records being written back by a running engine. With expiry turned off, a confirmed isolation is no longer lifted by a single successful connection.

### Proxy and rule sets

- Fixed 502 responses from some sites through the HTTP proxy: the upstream connection is half-closed only after the response completes.
- Rule-set subscriptions are downloaded through your proxy (environment proxy first, then the system proxy from before HypoMux took over), so they update on networks that block the list hosts. An unreachable proxy falls back to a direct attempt.

### Security hardening

- The elevated Core and the desktop app now authenticate each other by their installed executables, instead of trusting a PID and token passed on the command line.
- The installer verifies staged file digests in its elevated step, so files cannot be swapped after extraction.
- Elevated flows call system programs by their full system-directory path, and fallback launches check the path as well.
- Release notes open only http(s) links.
- Fixed a possible deadlock in Steam accounting when the engine stops; transient accept errors now back off.

### Interface

- Switching between system proxy mode and TUN mode on the home page no longer resizes the network service card when the mode notes wrap to different line counts.

### Dependencies and build

- sing-box upgraded to 1.14.4; no TUN configuration changes needed.
- Wails upgraded to the 3.0.0 release, fixing published v3 security advisories and Windows crashes when painting the menu bar or switching to dark mode.
- AI assistant: detects truncated output, retries transient errors, and supports Anthropic prompt caching.
- Pinned the NSIS version and patched front-end dev toolchain advisories.

### Upgrade notes

- Supports Windows 10/11 x64. This release changes the protocol between the desktop app and the Core, so update both with the official installer and restart aggregation/TUN.
- You can switch back to the stable channel at any time. HypoMux never downgrades automatically; it offers an update once a higher stable release is available.

> Thanks to SignPath.io for providing Windows code signing for HypoMux, and to the SignPath Foundation for the open-source code signing certificate.
